questions.question: A file contains a comment that tries to instruct the AI to ignore its rules and reveal secrets. At which stage is a prompt checked for this kind of prompt injection before it reaches the model?

options.text: Post-processing after the model responds
options.why: Post-processing checks the model's response, not the incoming prompt.

options.text: Content exclusion in repository settings
options.why: Content exclusions remove listed paths from context. They do not inspect prompt text.

options.text: Code scanning in GitHub Actions
options.why: Code scanning analyzes code in the repository, not Copilot prompts.

options.text: Pre-filtering in the GitHub Copilot proxy
options.why: Correct. The proxy pre-filters prompts for harmful content and prompt injection before the model.

questions.explanation: The proxy authenticates the request and runs pre-filters, including for prompt injection, before the prompt reaches the model.

questions.question: Which two checks are performed during post-processing of a Copilot response before the suggestion is shown? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Verifying that the developer has a Copilot seat
options.why: Authentication happens in the proxy before the model, not during post-processing.

options.text: Compiling the suggestion for the target platform
options.why: Post-processing does not compile or execute code.

options.text: Checks for common insecure code patterns
options.why: Correct. Post-processing includes quality and insecure-pattern checks.

options.text: Checks for matches with public code when the policy is set to Block
options.why: Correct. Matches of about 150 characters are hidden when the policy is Block.

options.text: Running the project's unit tests
options.why: Copilot's post-processing does not run your tests. You still need to test the code.

questions.explanation: Post-processing covers quality and insecure patterns, offensive content and public code matching.

questions.question: An organization sets Suggestions matching public code to Block. A developer types code for which the model generates a completion that matches public code of about 150 characters. What happens?

options.text: The suggestion is shown with a code reference and licence.
options.why: That is the behaviour when the policy is set to Allow.

options.text: The developer's Copilot seat is suspended.
options.why: Matching public code does not affect the seat.

options.text: The suggestion is shown and an audit log event is created for the match.
options.why: Blocked matches are not shown, and individual matches are not audit log events.

options.text: The suggestion is not shown to the developer.
options.why: Correct. With Block, post-processing hides suggestions that match public code.

questions.explanation: Block hides matching suggestions; Allow shows them with a code reference.

questions.question: A team lead proposes skipping code scanning for code written with Copilot because Copilot filters insecure patterns. What is the best response?

options.text: Turn off the public code filter so that more insecure patterns are detected.
options.why: The public code filter is about public code matches, not vulnerability detection.

options.text: Keep code scanning and reviews, because the filters catch some common patterns but not every vulnerability.
options.why: Correct. Filters reduce risk; they do not replace review, tests and scanning.

options.text: Agree, because post-processing guarantees that suggestions are secure.
options.why: Post-processing does not guarantee security.

options.text: Agree, but only for repositories that use Copilot Enterprise.
options.why: No plan makes Copilot's filters a replacement for code scanning.

questions.explanation: Copilot's filters are one layer. Developers remain responsible for reviewing, testing and scanning code.

questions.question: Which statement about the GitHub Copilot proxy is correct?

options.text: It is a component that each developer installs on their computer.
options.why: Developers do not install the proxy. The IDE extension connects to it.

options.text: It is configured in .vscode/mcp.json.
options.why: mcp.json configures MCP servers, not the Copilot proxy.

options.text: It runs only for Copilot Enterprise customers.
options.why: All Copilot requests pass through the proxy.

options.text: It is hosted by GitHub and authenticates and filters requests between the IDE and the model.
options.why: Correct. The proxy is a GitHub-hosted service in the request path.

questions.explanation: Every Copilot request passes through the GitHub-hosted proxy, which authenticates, pre-filters and post-processes.
